SEARCH

All Classes and Interfaces

Class
Description
App
Entry point of Phantom Maze.
Assets
Loads the Freedoom pictures from src/main/resources/freedoom/ and remembers them, so each file is read from disk only once.
Blast
A BFG explosion left where an enemy was blasted.
Combo
Counts a kill streak during a power-up.
Config
Central place for every tunable constant in the game (resolution, speeds, colors, ...), so no magic numbers are scattered through the code.
CursorWarp
Moves the mouse pointer to a screen position, used to keep it in the middle of the game.
CursorWarp.CGPoint
CoreGraphics' point type: two doubles.
CursorWarp.CGPoint.ByValue
Passed by value, as CGWarpMouseCursorPosition expects.
Difficulty
The difficulty levels picked on the main menu.
DoomFont
Doom's small red message font (the "STCFN" pictures).
Enemy
One Doom enemy (a Pac-Man "ghost").
Enemy.State
What the enemy is doing right now.
EnemyAI
Moves enemies through the maze using the original Pac-Man ghost rules: Enemies walk from tile center to tile center and only choose a new direction when they reach a center. They never turn straight around unless they hit a dead end (or the game tells them to with Enemy.reverse()). Each enemy picks a target tile and takes the step that leads there in the fewest steps.
EnemySprites
Picks the right Freedoom picture for an enemy: which animation frame (walking, hurt, dying) and which of the 8 viewing angles.
EnemyType
The four Doom enemies that replace Pac-Man's ghosts.
Game
Root of the game model.
GameFrame
The main application window.
GameLoop
Swing timer that reads input, updates the game, and repaints about 60 times a second.
GameMap
A rectangular tile grid parsed from text.
GamePanel
Panel that renders the game into a low-resolution off-screen image and scales it to the window.
GameState
The top-level states of the game.
HudRenderer
Draws everything on top of the 3D view: the gun in the player's hands, the crosshair, screen flashes, the Doom status bar (ammo of the held weapon, health, Doomguy's face, armor), pickup messages and the pause / game over screens.
InputController
Keyboard and mouse input for the game panel.
InputController.Actions
Actions that are decided by the screen controller.
MenuPanel
The main menu: pick a difficulty and mouse sensitivity, then start or quit.
MenuPanel.StartListener
Called when the player presses Start.
MinimapRenderer
Draws a top-down minimap with the player's position and view cone, the remaining dots and power-ups, and the enemies (only while the player has the shotgun power-up).
Patch
One Doom picture ("patch" in Doom terms): a sprite frame, a status bar digit, a face...
Pathfinder
Breadth-first search (BFS) over the tile grid.
Player
The player: position, facing, and camera plane, with wall-sliding movement.
Raycaster
Pure-math DDA ray caster against a GameMap.
RayHit
Mutable result of a ray cast; reused between casts to avoid per-frame allocation.
ScreenController
Switches between the menu and gameplay, and turns input actions into screen changes.
Sound
Every sound effect the game can ask for.
SoundListener
Receives the sounds the game wants to play.
SoundPlayer
Plays the game's sound effects with Java's built-in audio (javax.sound.sampled).
SpriteRenderer
Draws flat pictures that always face the camera ("billboards"): enemies and pickups.
TextureFactory
Generates the wall textures procedurally as packed RGB int arrays (no image files).
ThreatIndicator
The "sixth sense": when a dangerous enemy is close but the player cannot see it, the edge of the screen glows red on the side it will come from - left, right, bottom ("behind you"), or top ("around a corner ahead").
Vector2
A 2D point or direction with an x and a y value.
Weapon
The guns the player can hold.
Weapons
The player's guns: which one is held, how much ammo is left, and the timers that stop the player from shooting too fast or while reloading.
WorldRenderer
Draws the textured, fogged 3D walls plus the ceiling/floor gradient into an int[] pixel buffer.
